Article Title: Apple’s latest beta puts AI to work in conversations, at the gym and in the Health app
Article Text:
Apple Watch Showing the Wrong Time After Daylight Saving? How to Fix It

How much of a conversation is worth keeping?

A better reason to glance at the Watch between sets

Someone gives you an address. You catch the street name but miss the building number, and the conversation has already moved on. On the Apple Watch Series 12, a double press of the Digital Crown brings up the last 15 seconds as text. Apple calls it Live Rewind. Fifteen seconds sounds stingy until you think about how little of a conversation you usually need back.Live Rewind and Siri Recap have begun developer beta testing with iOS 27.3, with a public beta to follow. Both are opt-in features for the Series 12 and Ultra 4. Live Rewind has the clearer pitch. A glance at the wrist might be enough to recover a name or a number. The snippet disappears automatically unless it’s saved to the Siri app, and there’s an option to ask Siri about something in it.The double press also triggers a chime, even in silent mode, and an animation on the Watch. That makes an otherwise subtle gesture visible to the people around the wearer. It also gives the feature an interesting social wrinkle. In some conversations, it may still feel more natural to ask someone to repeat themselves.Siri Recap turns a conversation into a title and a short list of key points. Users can choose when and where it runs, and unsaved recaps are deleted within seven days.Apple says the feature does not identify speakers or retain raw audio. That makes it easier to see the appeal as a memory aid, though the lack of speaker attribution matters when the most important detail in a meeting is who agreed to do what.The real test for both features in India will be what happens when a conversation slips from English into Hindi, two people speak at once and a name or deadline gets buried in the middle. Live Rewind only has to recover a few words to be useful. Siri Recap has a harder job. It has to know which few words mattered.Fitness+ Gym Strength addresses a familiar gym problem. It’s easy to track how long a workout took. Figuring out what to lift today, and whether to go heavier than last week, takes more thought. Apple builds a four-week programme around the user’s goals, experience, schedule and available equipment, then adjusts it based on how training goes.The iPhone or iPad holds the plan and the exercise videos. On the Watch, users can check the next exercise, see the suggested reps and weight, and log what they actually managed. That division suits the gym. A video is worth pulling out the phone for when an exercise is unfamiliar. Checking whether the next set calls for eight reps or 12 should take a glance. The more revealing test will come when a three-session week turns into a one-session week and the plan has to adapt.The redesigned Health app, back in beta, offers a different sort of first impression. Health Age will probably get the first tap. It’s hard to resist finding out how old your phone thinks you are. The movement assessments have more potential to bring people back, especially if they can explain what’s changed over time in terms that help people decide how much to move or train.Gym Strength makes the strongest case for keeping the phone in the bag. Live Rewind is the more distinctive addition. After years of the Apple Watch tapping its wearer to deliver a notification, there’s finally an interesting reason to tap it back.
Article Summary: Live Rewind and Siri Recap have begun developer beta testing with iOS 27.3, with a public beta to follow. Both are opt-in features for the Series 12 and Ultra 4. Live Rewind only has to recover a few words to be useful. Siri Recap has to know which few words mattered.

Article Title: Nvidia director Mark Stevens and wife to donate $175 million to help build school in San Francisco's Bay Area that is first in a century and will focus on ...
Article Text:
School to focus on AI-powered healthcare

Partnership backed by major California institutions

Record gift, second big donation in 10 days

Nvidia wealth fuels giving

Mark Stevens, a board member of Nvidia Corp., and his wife Mary Stevens have pledged $175 million to help establish the first new medical school in the San Francisco Bay Area in more than 100 years, according to a joint announcement by Sutter Health and Santa Clara University. The new institution, named the Mark & Mary Stevens School of Medicine, will be developed through a partnership between the nonprofit healthcare system and the university. The school is planned for Santa Clara, located south of San Francisco and just a few miles from Nvidia's headquarters. The donation is the largest gift ever received by both organisations, as reported by Bloomberg.The future medical school will place a strong emphasis on the use of artificial intelligence in healthcare delivery. In a statement, Mark Stevens said the institution would be at the forefront of applying AI technologies to medicine and would help train the next generation of physicians and clinicians. The facility will span approximately 82,000 square feet and include classrooms, simulation facilities and an anatomy laboratory. Sutter Health expects the school to enrol about 120 students per class once it opens following a multi-year accreditation process.The school will be in Santa Clara, south of San Francisco and about two miles from Nvidia’s headquarters. Sutter Health said the 82,000-square-foot facility will have classrooms, simulation rooms and an anatomy lab. It expects to enrol about 120 students per class. The school will open only after a multiyear accreditation process.Mary Stevens, a graduate of Santa Clara University's 1984 class, has long supported the institution alongside her husband. The couple previously donated nearly $40 million for athletics facilities at the university. California Governor Gavin Newsom, who is also an alumnus of Santa Clara University, welcomed the initiative and described it as "a new model for medical education built to support a more innovative, connected healthcare system. "The gift is the largest ever received by both Santa Clara University and Sutter Health, a nonprofit. It comes 10 days after Stevens announced a $200 million donation to his alma mater, the University of Southern California. Stevens told Bloomberg that the USC money is meant to recruit faculty and bring AI into research across many fields, rather than to fund new buildings. Stevens joined Nvidia’s board in 1993, after an investment by his former venture firm, Sequoia Capital. That early bet has lifted his net worth to $13.9 billion, according to the Bloomberg Billionaires Index.Nvidia’s rise has produced several recent nine-figure gifts. In January, fellow director Tench Coxe gave $100 million from his $8.6 billion fortune to help launch a medical center at the University of Texas at Austin. CEO Jensen Huang, who has a fortune of $194.7 billion and ranks seventh richest in the world, had to give away $345 million from his foundation in 2025 to meet Internal Revenue Service requirements. He could owe nearly $500 million this year. The directors’ gifts have mostly gone to education and healthcare, two areas hit by federal funding cuts. Not every effort has succeeded. Huang gave $22.5 million in 2025 to try to save the California College of the Arts, but Vanderbilt University bought the struggling school in January.
Article Summary: Mark Stevens, a board member of Nvidia Corp., and his wife Mary Stevens have pledged $175 million to help establish the first new medical school in the San Francisco Bay Area in more than 100 years. The new institution, named the Mark & Mary Stevens School of Medicine, will be developed through a partnership between the nonprofit healthcare system and the university. The school is planned for Santa Clara, located south of San Francisco and just a few miles from Nvidia's headquarters.

Eric Schmidt believes AI could let large companies run with fewer employees. The former Google CEO said businesses could spend less time coordinating work, potentially eliminating roles focused on planning and administration. Speaking to Nicolai Tangen on the In Good Company podcast, he illustrated his argument with a hypothetical company employing 10,000 people.Schmidt said. Adopting AI would therefore require changes to how work is structured and managed, alongside the introduction of new software.

Article Title: Oracle 'dumps' $7 billion with one of China's biggest IT company after the US government reportedly tells the company: You cannot …
Article Text:
Oracle 'dumps' $7 billion with one of China's biggest IT company after the US government reportedly tells the company: You cannot …

Chinese AI companies turn to overseas data centres for advanced chips

Oracle has reportedly abandoned a multibillion-dollar chip with China’s Tencent after bowing to pressure from the US administration. According to a report by Financial Times, the California-based company signed a five-year lease with the leading Chinese tech giant to provide access to as many as 100,000 advanced AI chips across a host of data centres in south-east Asia. The contract was first reported by FT in September. Estimated to be worth $7 billion, it was Tencent’s largest overseas leasing deal. It would have given the group access to chips unavailable for use in China due to curbs from Washington and Beijing.As stated in the report, the US officials contacted Oracle raising concerns about the Tencent deal. People familiar with the matter told the publication that Tencent also received visits from top officials in Guangdong who asked the tech giant to support domestic Chinese chips.The deal has since been cancelled, the people added.China’s limited domestic supply of advanced chips, alongside tighter US export restrictions, has pushed technology companies to seek computing resources outside the country. Overseas leasing arrangements can provide access to Nvidia’s advanced processors, which Chinese companies cannot obtain directly for use in China.Chinese AI companies and leading AI labs are increasingly relying on these facilities to train their models, as domestic chips are not yet capable of handling such workloads at the same level.Although overseas chip-leasing deals remain permitted under existing rules, US companies are facing greater scrutiny over their exposure to Chinese clients. The FT also reported that Nvidia has asked cloud computing providers to ensure that at least 51% of their services are sold to non-Chinese customers.Tencent has been expanding its AI infrastructure spending as it seeks to narrow the gap with competitors. Its latest Hunyuan models have reportedly improved considerably, bringing them closer to leading Chinese models such as Alibaba’s Qwen.Meanwhile, ByteDance and Alibaba continue to be the largest customers of data centre capacity in Southeast Asia. Oracle has a major presence in the region, including several facilities in Malaysia that serve ByteDance. It also previously hosted US user data for TikTok before joining a consortium that acquired the app’s US operations late last year.
Article Summary: California-based company signed a five-year lease with the leading Chinese tech giant to provide access to as many as 100,000 advanced AI chips. The contract was first reported by FT in September. Estimated to be worth $7 billion, it was Tencent’s largest overseas leasing deal. It would have given the group access to chips unavailable for use in China.

Article Text:
Entire full-time police force in a Georgia city resigns; Milner Police Chief Lamar Bunn accuses city manager of putting GPS tracker in his truck; says in resignation letter: I have determined that it is …

What Police Chief Lamar Bunn said in his resignation letter

Why did the entire police force in Milner resign

What Police Chief Lamar Bunn alleged about GPS tracker

The entire full-time police force of Milner, a small city in Georgia, has resigned amid a growing dispute with city leadership. According to a report by Fox News Digital, Milner Police Chief Lamar Bunn has accused the city manager of secretly placing a GPS tracker on his truck, while alleging that concerns over legal compliance and ethical conduct have affected his ability to continue in the role. The city manager, Tausha Grose, has also announced her resignation, officials said during a city council meeting last month. The mass resignations include most of the city's part-time volunteer police officers, according to Grose. The developments have raised concerns over the future of the Milner Police Department, with officers calling for an investigation into the conduct of city leadership.In his resignation letter obtained by Fox News Digital, Bunn said he was stepping down because of fundamental differences with city leadership over governance, legal compliance and ethical standards.“I have determined that it is in my best interest to step down at this time due to fundamental differences regarding leadership, governance, and ethical alignment. Regrettably, recent actions and governance decisions within city leadership — specifically regarding legal compliance, ethical standards, and core values — have compromised my ability to perform my duties with integrity,” Bunn wrote.Milner Police Captain Craig Walton also called for an independent investigation into Mayor Craig Timmons.In his resignation letter, Walton urged residents and city council members to examine the mayor's conduct and possible violations of his oath of office or the rights of city employees.During the city council meeting, Tausha Grose announced that the full-time police department had resigned, along with most of its part-time officers. She also confirmed that she had submitted her own resignation to the city clerk.“It is with my extreme sorrow that our entire full-time police department has resigned, most of my part-time police. And also, I've also filed my resignation with the city clerk today,” Grose said.Several police department employees reportedly cited disagreements with the mayor and city council as the reason for leaving their positions.The city had also faced disputes over police overtime and a proposal to stop officers from using city vehicles for part-time work. However, these disagreements were not cited as the reason for the resignations.Milner Police Chief Lamar Bunn accused city hall of secretly placing a GPS tracker on his personal truck. He said the device was purchased using personal funds and installed without the knowledge of the city council or his supervisor. Bunn also said he had been falsely accused of having an affair with the city manager.During the meeting, he expressed uncertainty about whether he should continue working for the city, despite his long-standing connection to the area.“Here's the thing, still I'm looking for a glimmer of hope to stay in the city. I don't know why. It's because I've devoted my life to Lamar County. 15, 16 years with the sheriff's office and now I'm back here in this county. My dad was here in '74 policing with his police department. I got roots here,” Bunn said.Mayor Craig Timmons acknowledged the concerns raised during the city council meeting and said he hoped the situation could be resolved.as the city works to address the concerns raised by its former officers and city manager.
Article Summary: The entire full-time police force of Milner, a small city in Georgia, has resigned amid a growing dispute with city leadership. Milner Police Chief Lamar Bunn accused city hall of secretly placing a GPS tracker on his personal truck. He said the device was purchased using personal funds and installed without the knowledge of the city council or his supervisor.

Article Title: This US state is pushing to harness GPS technology to slow ‘super speeders’: How it works
Article Text:
Representative image

‘Ignition Interlock’ for excessive speed

How the GPS speed-limiting technology works

Drivers weaving through highway traffic at high speeds – often referred to by state officials as “super speeders” – may soon find their gas pedals physically resisting them. Virginia is pushing a first-in-the-nation enforcement initiative that uses GPS technology to cap how fast repeat offenders can drive. The move comes as speed continues to fuel a roadway crisis that federal data links to more than 10,000 fatalities nationwide each year, prompting several other states to consider similar interventions.The devices, officially known as Intelligent Speed Assistance (ISA), operate much like the ignition-interlock systems long mandated for drunken drivers. While alcohol interlocks require a clean breathalyzer test before an engine can turn over, ISA systems focus strictly on keeping dangerous driving habits in check. According to a report by The Wall Street Journal, since Virginia launched its pilot in July, roughly 100 speed-limiting devices have been installed in vehicles across the state.Most participants were charged with or convicted of reckless driving, frequently for clocking speeds topping 100 mph. Agreeing to have the device installed allows offenders to keep driving rather than face an outright driver’s license suspension.“We are talking about a small subset of drivers who are disproportionately causing harm on our roadways, and we finally have a tool that works. The big game-changer is that now all the roads are mapped for what their speed limits are,” said Amy Cohen, president of the advocacy group Families for Safe Streets.The technology pairs real-time satellite positioning with comprehensive digital mapping to regulate vehicle velocity. The onboard system uses GPS to determine exactly where the car is traveling. It then compares the vehicle’s location against an internal map database of posted legal speed limits. If a motorist hits the gas pedal in an attempt to exceed the legal limit, the device restricts the vehicle from going faster.Limited speed overrides remain built into the system, allowing drivers extra throttle for emergency maneuvers or highway merging.The rollout, however, has encountered several initial technical hurdles. According to one motorist's attorney, a faulty reading caused a device to abruptly restrict a vehicle to 35 mph while cruising on a highway, forcing the driver onto the shoulder. Another user reported that while driving through an intersection, their device mistakenly locked onto the lower speed limit of an adjacent cross street.State authorities and equipment manufacturers confirmed that these errors stem from “GPS drift”, a glitch where navigation hardware misidentifies a vehicle as traveling on a nearby frontage road or side street. Officials stated that an update addressing the problem will be deployed shortly.Enforcement rules around the equipment remain strict. State officials noted that one participant attempted to tamper with the unit, an act that carries potential criminal charges. That individual subsequently complied with program mandates and has since exited the initiative.
Article Summary: Virginia is pushing a first-in-the-nation enforcement initiative that uses GPS technology to cap how fast repeat offenders can drive. The move comes as speed continues to fuel a roadway crisis that federal data links to more than 10,000 fatalities nationwide each year.

Article Title: ‘This should not have happened’: Binance says North Korean hackers used LinkedIn to trap engineer into the history’s biggest crypto theft
Article Text:
“This should not have happened, and we apologise for the concern, disruption and uncertainty it caused our users, partners and the wider industry,”

How fake recruiters targeted the engineer on LinkedIn

“Software Engineer B was contacted through a legitimate job-hunting platform by an individual posing as a Project Director. Software Engineer B's profile on the platform referenced his experience at Binance. The purported Project Director arranged a first-round interview with a HR representative, followed by a second-round interview with an individual claiming to be the CEO of a fictitious company,”

A malicious advertisement provided another opening

What Binance says it recovered

Binance has revealed that fake job interviews on LinkedIn helped hackers steal $6.3 billion from its crypto accounts. The cryptocurrency exchange has reportedly disclosed that North Korean attackers approached an engineer on LinkedIn, staged interviews with supposed company representatives and persuaded the employee to download a malicious assignment. According to Binance, the recruitment scheme, combined with an earlier attack on another engineer, gave hackers access to wallets in what it described as the biggest theft in crypto history.Binance said in a statement seen by Fortune. The company said the operation unfolded over several months, using social engineering to manipulate people into sharing information or taking unsafe actions, along with malicious software.Binance said an individual posing as a project director contacted an engineer whose professional profile mentioned experience at the exchange.the company noted.The staged recruitment process led the engineer to download an assignment that let the attackers into the company's systems, executives told reporters.A Binance spokesperson said employees in roles that do not involve public-facing work are prohibited from maintaining LinkedIn profiles. The spokesperson declined to clarify whether the engineer had breached that policy or whether either employee involved would be dismissed.The attackers had earlier targeted a different engineer through an online advertisement promoting a tampered version of Homebrew, a tool used to install and manage software. According to Binance, the employee downloaded it through the advertisement rather than the company’s approved channels.Binance said it detected and removed the malicious software. However, the attackers had already obtained information about the engineer’s responsibilities and other employees who managed company wallets.The company said that information, combined with the fake recruitment operation, enabled the hackers to take control of several wallets and drain funds. Binance said it had previously detected and prevented 57 North Korea-related hacking attempts in 2026.The theft took place over several hours last week. Binance suspended withdrawals for approximately 48 hours before restoring them.The exchange said it recovered around $2.5 billion of the $6.3 billion stolen after Tether and Circle froze stolen stablecoins, cryptocurrencies designed to track the value of assets such as the US dollar.Separately, Binance said it had replenished 98% of the stolen coins using reserves and other sources, while maintaining that customer funds were safe. It was still acquiring the remaining 2%, consisting of less widely used currencies.
Article Summary: Binance says fake job interviews on LinkedIn helped hackers steal $6.3 billion from its crypto accounts. North Korean attackers approached an engineer on LinkedIn, staged interviews with supposed company representatives and persuaded the employee to download a malicious assignment. The recruitment scheme, combined with an earlier attack on another engineer, gave hackers access to wallets in what it described as the biggest theft in crypto history.

Article Title: Chip smuggler details how a single loophole is letting banned South Korean RAM slip into China’s AI labs
Article Text:
High Bandwidth Memory

How high-cost, banned memory is ‘shipped’ into China

Prices skyrocket as AI race accelerates

Advanced memory chips barred under strict export controls are slipping across borders directly into Chinese artificial intelligence (AI) laboratories, guided by a regulatory blind spot in international trade rules, a report has said. A memory smuggler has reportedly revealed how export-controlled High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) manufactured in South Korea by Samsung and SK Hynix reaches mainland China. Under current US and South Korean trade restrictions, standalone exports of cutting-edge HBM units to China are outright prohibited. Yet the smuggler, who runs a chip design venture, identified an easy detour around the embargo, The Information reports.The report (via Tom’s Hardware) details that regulatory export controls measure only the raw computing performance of the server processor itself, without evaluating secondary components attached to the board. By designing cheap, low-performing processors that sit comfortably beneath the legal restriction limits, the firm attaches premium Samsung and SK Hynix HBM directly onto the modules. As the central processor is deemed harmless under export criteria, the full board clears customs inspections without raising red flags.Transporting the hardware into mainland China involves a delicate process. Firstly, the low-end boards with top-tier memory first arrive in Hong Kong. From there, daily commuters carry the hardware inside personal luggage across the border into Shenzhen. Once inside Shenzhen, the hardware is taken to local workshops. Technicians heat the circuit boards to soften the solder, carefully pry off the valuable HBM units and throw away the cheap processors and host boards.Even though melting and lifting memory off boards carries a high failure rate, the surging street value of functional HBM units makes the risky operation profitable.The black market for advanced memory has expanded rapidly alongside China’s push to train competitive AI models. A Shenzhen-based broker facilitating transactions between smugglers and hardware-starved domestic tech firms noted that street prices have reached historic highs.“A year ago, a single HBM3E unit changed hands in China for several hundred dollars. Today it’s about $4,000,” the broker told The Information.Modern AI accelerators require between six and eight high-end memory units to operate. At current black-market rates, brokers generate $24,000 to $32,000 for the memory bundle needed to run a single AI graphics processing unit (GPU).
Article Summary: A memory smuggler has reportedly revealed how export-controlled High Bandwidth Memory (HBM) reaches mainland China. Under current US and South Korean trade restrictions, standalone exports of cutting-edge HBM units to China are outright prohibited. The smuggler, who runs a chip design venture, identified an easy detour around the embargo.

Article Title: From bumper discounts to ‘free gifts’: How to spot festive online shopping scams
Article Text:
Bumper discounts that don’t add up

“Free gift” links and fake contests

Fake shopping sites and apps

Fake delivery and customer-care messages

Safer shopping habits

What to do if you’ve been scammed

The festive season is the busiest time of the year for online shopping, and also for online fraud. As sale banners go up and deal alerts flood phones, scammers move in with their own versions: websites that copy famous brands, discounts that seem too generous to pass up, and “free gift” links that arrive on WhatsApp just when people are hunting for bargains. The pressure and excitement to lock a deal before it disappears often makes it easy to click first and think later. Also, many of such traps look convincing as they come with real logos, polished pages and some urgent countdowns which compel you to click. Knowing the warning signs can save you from losing money, card details or access to your accounts. Here is how to tell a genuine festive offer from a fake one.A latest-model smartphone at half price, or a branded watch for a few hundred rupees, should make you stop and think. Genuine sales do cut prices, but fraudsters set theirs absurdly low because they never plan to deliver. Compare the price with the same product on the brand’s official store or a trusted marketplace. If it is far lower than everywhere else, treat it as a warning. Countdown timers and “only three left” banners are also pressure tactics, and they are easy for anyone to fake.We often receive messages announcing that we have won some festive hamper, or a voucher or even a gold coin in some lucky draw.But what is important here is that we never participated in any such draw and its always turn out to be a scam. The link which is shared in the message may direct you to a form which asks for your address, credit card details and may also charge small ‘shipping fee’. But it’s important that you never pay to receive a prize. Also, keep in mind that you never need a UPI PIN or an OTP to receive money or a gift, because those are used only to send payments or confirm them. If a page asks for either, close it.Scammers always try to lure the customers by creating copycat websites with addresses that are slightly off. For instance, they may include some extra words, a swapped letter or an unusual ending. So, before to make any purchase just thoroughly check the web address and look for contact details and a clear return policy. Also, be cautious about the pages that accept only payment made by UPI transfer or bank transfer. Avoid downloading ant app from the links shared in chats or text messages. It’s important that you always download and install the apps only from the official Play Store or App Store, as the fake files present in forwarded messages can steal your data and also read all your messages.During the time of festive sale, many of use receive text messages saying that your parcel is stuck and you will have to pay a small amount or update your address details by clicking on the given link. Scammers also post fake customer-care numbers on social media and search results, then ask you to share an OTP or install a screen-sharing app in order to fix the order. It’s important to note that the real companies never ask for any of these details. You can always check your order status inside the shopping app and can find the customer care number by visiting the official website of the company.* It is advisable to type the complete website address by yourself or always access the service via its official app and avoid clicking on any random link present in a message.* Always use the platform’s official checkout system. Cards or cash on delivery can offer more protection than a direct transfer to an individual.* Always keep a check on the reviews of the service. Some of the glowing reviews can be fake, so read a mix and check when they were posted online.* It’s always important to stay alert. So, enable two-step verification, and use a different password for each shopping account.* In case an offer makes you feel rushed, check it with the brand before paying.Act fast. Call your bank immediately to block your card or account, and change the passwords on any accounts you may have exposed. Uninstall any app you were told to download. In India, report the fraud on the national cybercrime helpline 1930 or at cybercrime.gov.in, as early reporting improves the chances of freezing the money. Report and block the sender, and warn friends and family.A good rule for the season is simple: if the deal seems too good to be true, or you can’t verify it, walk away.
Article Summary: The festive season is the busiest time of the year for online shopping. As sale banners go up and deal alerts flood phones, scammers move in with their own versions. Knowing the warning signs can save you from losing money, card details or access to your accounts.

Article Title: One of the biggest telecom companies in UK is cutting thousands of jobs, changes fibre network expansion plan
Article Text:
Virgin Media O2 is set to cut thousands of jobs

CEO says ‘tough but necessary’ reset

Shifting fibre and network strategy

British telecoms giant Virgin Media O2 is set to cut thousands of jobs and pull back on its fibre expansion plans as it faces fierce competition in the UK broadband and mobile markets. The company, jointly owned by Liberty Global and Telefonica, announced Tuesday that it aims to save £800 million by 2029, as per a report by news agency Reuters. To hit that target, the company plans to slash its wage bill by 30%, with the bulk of the reductions focused on non-customer-facing roles. The report said that Virgin Media O2 currently employs around 15,000 people.The restructuring comes as the operator faces pressure from rival BT’s nationwide fibre rollout, as well as dozens of smaller alternative networks ("alt-nets") winning over subscribers with faster, lower-cost broadband connections.Virgin Media O2 CEO Lutz Schüler described the cuts as unavoidable given current market dynamics. He said: “Given the market conditions we face, the regulatory backdrop in fibre and the technological changes sweeping across all areas of the economy, standing still and doing what we’ve always done is not an option”.In the third quarter, Virgin Media O2 shed 23,300 fixed-line customers, bringing its customer base down to 5.5 million.Total revenue fell 5.7% to £2.4 billion ($3.22 billion), while adjusted core earnings slid 2.6% to £995 million.The company had previously aimed to overhaul its legacy cable network with full fibre and grow its reach by purchasing Netomnia, one of the UK’s largest alt-nets. However, the UK competition regulator blocked the proposed deal last month.In light of the regulatory pushback, Virgin Media O2 stated that market conditions do not justify building “three overlapping fibre networks.” Instead of continuing aggressive proprietary builds, the company is adjusting its infrastructure playbook.Firstly, it will upgrade its current cable infrastructure, using older technology, to deliver 2Gbps speeds to most customers next year. Further, any future fibre investments deemed strategically sound will be financed off-balance sheet and limited strictly to areas where alt-nets are not present.The company also said it is exploring wholesale arrangements to deliver services in regions outside the footprint of its own lines and Nexfibre’s network.
Article Summary: Virgin Media O2 is set to cut thousands of jobs and pull back on its fibre expansion plans. The company, jointly owned by Liberty Global and Telefonica, announced Tuesday that it aims to save £800 million by 2029. The restructuring comes as the operator faces pressure from rival BT’s nationwide fibre rollout.

Article Title: US charges 13 Brazilians and Cubans for running fake immigration firm in Florida; what court documents show
Article Text:
US charges 13 Brazilians and Cubans for running fake immigration firm in Florida; what court documents show

Charges against 13 foreign nations accused by US

What the court documents show

Thirteen nationals from Brazil and Cuba have been charged in the US for allegedly running a fake immigration services firm in Florida. As stated in an official release by the Department of Justice, the accused allegedly provided false legal advice, falsified immigration documents and helped clients fraudulently obtain immigration benefits. According to court documents, the company, Legacy Imigra Solutions LLC, allegedly posed as a professional immigration firm staffed by experts and attorneys to attract clients. The defendants also allegedly hired immigrants they knew were not authorised to work in the US and conspired to commit marriage fraud.Vagner Sorares De Almeida (age 54), Juliana Colucci (age 47), Lucas Felipe Trindade Silva (age 34), and Ronaldo De Campos (age 35) are each charged with one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud and two counts of wire fraud. They are also charged with four counts of conspiracy to commit visa fraud, one count of conspiracy to commit marriage fraud, and one count of unlawful employment of aliens.Erick Bruno Goncalves De Assis Pinto (age 34), Nathalia Da Costa Ferreira (age 43), Nathalia Gomes Ciriaco (age 29), and Kelen Cristina Da Silva (age 37) are each charged with charged with one count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud, two counts of wire fraud, and four counts of conspiracy to commit visa fraud.Issac Antonio Narvaez (age 69) is charged with three counts of conspiracy to commit marriage fraud.Ronay Castillo Salazar (age 51), Rebeca Aldama Garcia (age 40), Mijail Cabera Nunez (age 52), and Lorraine Soares Oliverira (age 32) are each charged with one count of conspiracy to commit marriage fraud.According to court records, from August 18, 2023, through April 20, 2026, Vagner Sorares De Almeida owned and operated a corporate entity registered in Florida called Legacy Imigra Solutions LLC (“Legacy”). Juliana Colucci, Lucas Felipe Trindade Silva, Nathalia Da Costa Ferreira, Nathalia Gomes Ciriaco, Ronaldo De Campos, Erick Bruno Goncalves De Assis Pinto, and Kelen Cristina Da Silva were employees of the company. Legacy falsely purported to be a professional establishment employed by immigration experts and attorneys who could assist individuals with immigration-related legal work. It was part of the conspiracy to give false, inaccurate, and incomplete legal and immigration advice to prospective clients to induce them to retain Legacy’s services. Legacy would falsify immigration documents to fraudulently obtain immigration status and benefits for their clients. The defendants also engaged in a regular practice of hiring aliens knowing that the individuals were unauthorized for employment in the United States. Vagner Sorares De Almeida, Juliana Colucci, Ronay Castillo Salazar, Rebeca Aldama Garcia, Mijail Cabera Nunez, Lorraine Soares Oliverira, and Issac Antonio Narvaez also conspired to commit marriage fraud.If convicted, each count of conspiracy to commit wire fraud and wire fraud carries a maximum penalty of 20 years’ imprisonment. The conspiracy to commit visa fraud offenses are each punishable up to 10 years’ imprisonment. The maximum penalty for conspiracy to commit marriage fraud is 5 years in federal prison, and unlawful employment of aliens carries a maximum penalty of 6 months’ imprisonment.The investigation is part of the Homeland Security Task Force (HSTF).
Article Summary: Thirteen nationals from Brazil and Cuba have been charged in the US for allegedly running a fake immigration services firm in Florida. The accused allegedly provided false legal advice, falsified immigration documents and helped clients fraudulently obtain immigration benefits. The defendants also allegedly hired immigrants they knew were not authorised to work in the U.S.

Article Title: Hinge is testing a cheaper plan to get more users to pay
Article Text:
File image: Hinge

Hinge’s payers are growing, but each one is worth less

Hinge is testing a cheaper subscription plan, Match Group said on its Q3 2026 earnings call on Monday. The new tier adds extra filters and custom location boundaries, giving users more say over who they see and where they meet them.CFO Steve Bailey said the plan is designed for women in particular, along with price-sensitive users. He didn’t reveal the price. It’s also a U-turn of sorts, since Hinge tried a pricier tier in 2023.Bailey’s reasoning was simple. Hinge is one of Match’s costliest products, with revenue per payer nearly double Tinder’s. But its payer penetration is only slightly more than half of Tinder’s. People who pay, pay well. Too few pay.Hinge made $31.81 per payer a month in Q3, against $18.02 at Tinder. Payers rose 23 percent to 2.3 million, though Tinder still has 8.9 million. Revenue per payer slipped 3 percent year on year, and from $33.11 in Q2, as the base swelled. A cheaper plan could push it lower.Hinge isn’t struggling, though. Monthly active users grew 12 percent. Direct revenue, which covers subscriptions and in-app purchases, jumped 19 percent to $221 million, and operating income climbed 52 percent to $70 million.Tinder’s direct revenue slipped 2 percent to $480 million, with payers down 4 percent.That strength gives Match room to experiment. Dating app users are tired of subscriptions, endless swiping and a so-so overall experience, and many question whether premium features are worth the money. A lower entry price could win some of them over without a big upfront ask.Match is also trying to make its apps feel less like dating apps. Group Hangouts and Events are live, and the company will ramp them up in Q4. Real-time adaptive recommendations for Tinder start testing then too, reacting to user actions in seconds rather than hours.
Article Summary: Hinge made $31.81 per payer a month in Q3, against $18.02 at Tinder. Payers rose 23 percent to 2.3 million, though Tinder still has 8.9 million. A lower entry price could win some of them over without a big upfront ask.

Article Title: UK will face AI cyberattacks on critical infrastructure by 2028, official says
Article Text: LONDON: The United Kingdom will likely face artificial intelligence cyberattacks on its critical infrastructure by 2028 as criminals and states, including China and Russia, increasingly use AI in their cyberactivity, Britain’s cyberchief said Tuesday.That could include AI-powered malware for ransomware attacks as the technology will allow “vulnerabilities that have been tolerated for far too long” to be discovered and exploited “at a scale that was once unimaginable,” said Richard Horne, the head of the National Cyber Security Center.One such vulnerability was discovered in refrigeration units that were targeted by hackers who turned up the temperature, causing food to thaw.The U.K. has also been affected, Horne said.In a speech marking the publication of the annual cyber report by the National Cyber Security Center, or NCSC, Horne said that the leaders of businesses and organizations of all sizes who have “got away with tech on the cheap” will have to explain why “food isn’t on the shelves, lights aren’t on, businesses have gone under,” if they fail to invest in cybersecurity or update out-of-date technology.Chinese cyberactivity is the “most sophisticated and sustained cyber challenge facing the U.K.” while both Russia and China will routinely use AI to achieve their geopolitical goals, the report said. Russia is intentionally conducting cybercampaigns which fall below the threshold of armed conflict, while Iran is carrying out attacks against the U.K. and targeting individuals who are a threat to the Iranian government, Horne said.The use of AI by states and criminals is highly likely to increase the scale and efficiency of hostile operations, but AI is more likely to be used to enhance and scale existing tactics and techniques rather than find brand new vulnerabilities, the report said.Technology “underpins the automation of physical processes that are vital to modern life,” Horne said. That includes, he said, electricity switching, sluice gates in water facilities, dam operations, manufacturing lines, heating and refrigeration controls. The recent cyberattacks on refrigeration systems in French supermarkets showed how easily hostile actors could exploit civilian infrastructure, Horne said.Fridges across Europe have been affected, including in the U.K., where security experts from the NCSC worked “through the night” to contact organizations with the vulnerable technology, Horne told The Associated Press.Refrigeration systems in France were attacked because they were using old technology which was no longer being updated and that was connected directly to the internet with default passwords, Horne said. It was, he said, not an AI attack but one where bad actors exploited vulnerabilities that have existed for a long time and showed the need for businesses to address the security of operational technology.Last week, governments and corporations worked on urgent security updates after the AI-assisted discovery of vulnerabilities in a programming language vital to 70% of websites globally. The two critical flaws identified by AI could allow bad actors to get unauthenticated access to sites which, in theory, could allow them to control a web server remotely without needing a password.Russia has already attacked critical infrastructure in Europe, according to the U.K. and European Union member states that said Russia’s FSB security service was behind an attack on Poland’s energy grid in December 2025. If the attack had been successful, 500,000 people could have lost electricity during winter.In the U.K., malicious cyberactivity is costing organizations almost $20 billion every year, the NCSC said. In 2025, the carmaker Jaguar Land Rover suffered more than $260 million in direct losses following a cyberattack which also hit suppliers and dented the U.K. economy.“We need every organization in the U.K. to take action now. Not only to protect their customers, services and livelihoods, but because cybersecurity is now part of the front-line defense of our nation,” said Anne Keast-Butler, director of GCHQ, Britain’s signals intelligence agency, which the NCSC is part of.
Article Summary: Criminals and states, including China and Russia, increasingly use AI in their cyberactivity, Britain's cyberchief says. Technology will allow “vulnerabilities that have been tolerated for far too long’ to be discovered and exploited “at a scale that was once unimaginable,” Richard Horne says.

Article Title: Anthropic adds new rule to Claude Code for game clones; company says: Using Claude to infringe IP is against our...
Article Text:
Anthropic’s Claude Code and Opus 5.5 now block video game cloning

AI game clones had already become a headache for developers

Claude is now left to judge what counts as a clone

Anthropic has added a new rule to Claude Code that stops the AI coding tool from recreating existing video games, even if a user renames the copy or calls it original. The two-sentence instruction tells Claude to build original games, games in a genre and games from a user’s own designs and assets, but not a recreation of a specific title.Anthropic engineer Addy Osmani confirmed the change on October 30. He said the sentences were added to Claude Code’s prompt on Opus 5.5 because using Claude to infringe IP is against the company’s usage policy. Original games should keep working, he added, and anyone wrongly refused can send the case to him.The rule was first spotted by an X user called chasm, who traced it to a flag named “tengu_heron_brook” that reached Claude Code around October 27. There is reportedly no setting to switch it off. The text also sits inside Claude Code version 2.1.314, while separate Opus 5.5 settings suggest the model can receive the guidance on its own.The timing is not random. Steam Next Fest last month was flooded with low-effort games, and itch.io has reportedly seen the number of new game pages double in two months. Some studios chose to hide their work. Alliance Arts and Who You pulled the Drunken Goddess Reflux demo despite 25,000 wishlists, while Digital Sun moved ReVamp to a private Discord playtest.The reverse engineering community has felt it too. Game decompilation hub decomp.dev shut down last month, with its maintainer saying fast AI tools had turned a patient community effort into a numbers race.That is where the trouble starts. Independent tests found that Opus 5.5 still agreed to help with a decompilation and a static recompilation of Pokemon Diamond, treating both as different from rebuilding the game. Developers report otherwise elsewhere. One filed a GitHub issue after Claude refused to help build board-wargame modules for paying customers, made from games those customers own.Reverse engineering tasks are also being refused. A developer testing his own software found that switching to Opus 4.8 let his work continue, and a Reddit user said their account was suspended over Opus 5.5 and a reverse engineering tool, then reinstated.The rule also leaves open questions. A straight copy of Tetris would be blocked, but a game in the Tetris genre should pass. Where a mashup, such as Mario dropped into Elden Ring, falls is anyone’s guess. Claude is left to judge that on its own, with only two sentences to go on.Workarounds are easy, too. Anyone set on cloning a game can move to rival coding tools or open-weight models that have no such rule. Anthropic has also not said whether the rule will extend to its other models.For now, the rule blocks the easiest request, a named game rebuilt from scratch. It does little to stop a determined copier, and it has already caught some developers working on their own projects.
Article Summary: Claude is now left to judge what counts as a clone. Anthropic has not said whether the rule will extend to its other models. It does little to stop a determined copier and it has already caught some developers working on their own projects.

Article Title: Anthropic and OpenAI ban employees from wearing company badges outside office; give 'guidelines' on friendship, romance as they become targets of ...
Article Text:
OpenAI warns staff about approaches outside work

“Everyone wants to find out about developments and information at the cutting edge of technology. They want firsthand information. They want to talk to these employees, but the employees generally avoid discussing anything,”

Protests and attacks add to security concerns

Employees’ families describe concerns about trust

“I also pay attention to safety and remind my child to be careful, because he can easily become a target. They try not to talk about their work at all. They keep it more about sports, hobbies, hiking and food,”

“Whether you’re going to a party, looking for a partner or making friends, people focus on your company and your wealth,”

“They overlook your character and your values.”

Anthropic and OpenAI are reportedly telling employees to conceal company badges and logos in public. According to the New York Post, OpenAI has instructed staff not to wear items carrying its logo outside the office, while Anthropic reminds workers to hide their badges and has largely restricted branded merchandise. The precautions come amid concerns about espionage, unwanted approaches and hostility towards people working in artificial intelligence (AI).OpenAI’s security training warns that spies may offer money, friendship or romance to obtain confidential information. The guidance reportedly concerns attempts to exploit personal relationships, not a ban on employees forming them. Anthropic has also reported people trying to photograph its offices, adding to concerns about how easily workers can be identified.OpenAI’s security sessions describe methods ranging from overhearing conversations in cafes to bribery and attempts to build personal relationships. In one incident reported by The Wall Street Journal, a stranger approached an OpenAI employee at a San Francisco playground and gradually steered the conversation towards work. The publication claimed that the person was a spy. Employees are also reminded to use privacy screens on public transport and erase meeting-room whiteboards before leaving.Miao Hong, managing partner of Silicon Valley Future Capital and an investor in both companies, said that people repeatedly approach AI workers seeking inside information.he said.The precautions also come against a backdrop of hostility towards AI companies and their employees. In March, activists wrote messages outside OpenAI’s San Francisco offices urging staff to quit over its Pentagon agreement. OpenAI CEO Sam Altman’s home was targeted in two separate incidents in April 2026, according to the report.One suspect allegedly threw a Molotov cocktail at the property and subsequently threatened OpenAI’s headquarters. Two other suspects were accused of firing a shot outside his home two days later. All three were arrested and charged, pleaded not guilty and are awaiting trial.Meanwhile, Anthropic disclosed in its stock-market listing filing that it spent $2.7 million on personal security services for CEO Dario Amodei, the report added.The father of an Anthropic employee, who asked not to be named, said that his son and colleagues avoid discussing work socially.he said.He also described the difficulty of judging whether new acquaintances were interested in his son personally or in his employer.he said.
Article Summary: Anthropic and OpenAI are reportedly telling employees to conceal company badges and logos in public. The precautions come amid concerns about espionage, unwanted approaches and hostility towards people working in artificial intelligence. OpenAI’s security training warns that spies may offer money, friendship or romance to obtain confidential information. Anthropic has also reported people trying to photograph its offices.

Article Title: Nvidia tells data centre clients to sell majority of services to non-Chinese buyers; company says: 'Datacenters and clouds built on American chips are the foundation...'
Article Text:
Nvidia tells cloud clients to cut China exposure

Chinese AI firms relied on overseas cloud leases to train models

Banned Nvidia B300 racks now sell for far more in China

Nvidia has told its data centre partners that most of their services must go to non-Chinese customers, a new rule that narrows China's routes to advanced AI computing power, according to a Financial Times report.The chipmaker has asked cloud computing clients to sell at least 51% of their services to companies outside China, five people familiar with the matter told FT. There were no such limits earlier. The instructions were passed on verbally by Nvidia's sales and regional teams rather than put in writing.The rule applies to Nvidia's clients globally, not just those in Asia, two of the sources said. It covers only future contracts, so existing leasing agreements stay as they are.In a statement, Nvidia said data centres and clouds built on American chips form the base on which American model and application makers compete worldwide, and that long-standing US policy supports building American infrastructure abroad.Many Chinese tech groups rented advanced computing power from data centres outside the country, including for training AI models. Washington is now going after both the middlemen who feed the black market for Nvidia chips in China and these overseas leasing deals.Cloud providers are already struggling to comply. One Singapore-based group told FT it is hard to find enough non-Chinese customers outside the US, and that strict enforcement would hurt business. Data centres that cannot find them could have to shrink their operations.Scarcity is already showing in prices. A rack of B300 chips fetched nearly five times its international price in China last month, a person with direct knowledge of the deal told FT. The B300 cannot be sold in China under US export controls and is used by American AI players such as Anthropic and OpenAI.Nvidia has also more than halved the number of Asian customers allowed to buy its AI chips this year, after creating a white list of companies that cleared tougher compliance checks. That pushed more Chinese firms towards overseas leasing, the route the new rule now targets.Nvidia shares have fallen more than 13% in the past month, and Apple has now overtaken it as the world's most valuable listed company.The body runs to about 380 words. I named FT as you asked, and I left out the dollar and yuan figures for the B300 since your style calls for INR and I didn't want to guess at a conversion rate. If you'd like the rupee figure in, give me the rate you use and I'll add it.
Article Summary: N Nvidia tells cloud clients to cut China exposure. Chinese AI firms relied on overseas cloud leases to train models. Washington is now going after both the middlemen who feed the black market for Nvidia chips in China and these overseas leasing deals. Cloud providers are already struggling to comply.

Article Title: 143-year-old Pittsburgh paint company finds its biggest boom as Microsoft, Google, Amazon build AI data centres; gray paint sales to data centres set to triple; VP says: “I’ve never seen a…
Article Text:
Fans that are part of a cooling system are seen on the roof of a data center, Monday, April 27, 2026, in Hillsboro, Ore. (AP Photo/Jenny Kane)

Data centre paint sales are outrunning PPG's overall growth

Steelguard 951 swells into a crust that keeps fire away from steel

PPG, a 143-year-old Pittsburgh company that started out making glass, has found an unlikely growth engine in AI data centres. The firm expects its paint sales to data centres to triple this year from last year, The New York Times reported. The coatings are mostly gray and they do a serious job, shielding steel from fire, rust and static electricity inside the huge facilities that Microsoft, Google, Amazon and other tech giants are racing to build. "I've never seen a boom as big as this," said Jenn Solcz, PPG's vice president of protective and marine coatings for the Americas.The surge stands out against the rest of the business. PPG's total sales rose 7% to $4.5 billion in the most recent quarter, and data centres still make up only a low-single-digit share of sales in two parts of the company, executives told the Times.Amy Ericson, a PPG senior vice president, expects data centres to grow "multiple times" faster than other infrastructure markets.Rival Sherwin-Williams is seeing a similar pull. Its chief executive, Heidi Petz, said in July that its protective and marine sales rose by a midteens percentage from a year earlier, helped by data centre construction.Speed is a big part of the pitch. Data centres go up in about a third of the time a typical infrastructure project takes, Solcz said, so PPG built one team for the tech giants and another that works with architects and builders before construction begins.The aim is to get its coatings written into a project's approved materials list early.In April, PPG rolled out a data centre package at a trade show in Washington. It covers steel fireproofing, rust-resistant primers, anti-static flooring and coatings that block electrical interference between machines. The company also makes coatings for more than 75 data centre parts, including security camera housings and cooling equipment.The flagship product is Steelguard 951. At PPG's test facility near Pittsburgh, researchers aimed torches at coated steel panels inside a concrete building called "the bunker." Paul Fenton, a PPG chemist, held up one panel where a 1 mm layer of paint had swollen into a black crust almost 10 mm tall. Trapped air keeps the steel cool, he said, "just like a toasted marshmallow."The coating can protect steel for up to four hours, which gives people time to get out. Fires at data centres can start at backup generators, batteries or nearby power plants.Looks barely matter. PPG's shades are named light gray, gray and dark gray, and data centres are filled with machines, not people. Pipes are the exception, with blue for chilled water and red for sprinklers. Matthew Giddings of real estate firm JLL said paint can cost $3 million to $8 million for one building, a sliver of construction costs.There are bumps ahead. Some projects are waiting on power, transformer shortages have stretched timelines, and local opposition is growing. In 2024, it sold its US and Canadian paint-store business, including the Glidden brand, and now mostly serves businesses, coating cars, aircraft and beverage cans.

Article Title: Apple’s India story is getting bigger: Record iPhone upgrades, Mac sales and services revenue
Article Text:
FILE - The Apple logo is illuminated at a store in Munich, Germany, April 2, 2026. (AP Photo/Matthias Schrader, File)

The iPhone still brings customers back to Apple in India and perhaps is the gateway to the hallowed ecosystem from Cupertino. The September quarter offered a glimpse of what else they might buy once they’re there. Apple posted its highest-ever quarterly revenue in the country, with Macs and services also setting all-time India records. At the same time, CEO John Ternus said more people in India upgraded their iPhones than in any previous September quarter.Put those numbers together and there’s a more interesting story than another strong quarter for the iPhone. Apple has three ways to grow in India: sell an existing customer their next iPhone, persuade them to consider a Mac when they need a laptop, and earn from services in the years between those purchases. The earnings call showed strength in all three. It didn’t tell us how often the same customer was doing all three.The Mac record is particularly interesting because it works in both directions. An iPhone owner shopping for a laptop may give the MacBook Neo a look because it costs less than other MacBooks and works with a phone they already own. For someone replacing a Windows laptop who has never owned an Apple device, the Neo could be their first purchase from the company.Either would widen Apple’s reach in India in a way that selling a new Mac to someone replacing an old one wouldn’t.CFO Kevan Parekh credited the MacBook Neo and MacBook Pro for global Mac revenue growth of 24% to $10.8 billion. Apple didn’t say which models drove the India record or how many buyers were new to the Mac. That is the detail to watch: a strong quarter for the Pro and a quarter in which the Neo wins over first-time Mac buyers can both produce record revenue, but only one tells you that Apple is reaching people who might never have considered a Mac.Services add another dimension. Someone can keep the same iPhone for years and still pay Apple every month for iCloud storage or spend money on the App Store. Globally, services brought in $31.6 billion, up 10% and more than a quarter of Apple’s $114.5 billion in quarterly revenue. Apple hasn’t said how close India is to that mix, or whether its local record came from more paying customers, higher spending by existing users or other sources of revenue.For years, a good quarter for Apple in India was easiest to read through the iPhone. That’s still where much of the attention will go. But the Mac and services records give us two more things to watch: whether Apple is becoming a serious option when Indians shop for a laptop, and what customers are willing to pay for after they’ve bought the device.
Article Summary: Apple posted its highest-ever quarterly revenue in the country, with Macs and services also setting all-time India records. Apple has three ways to grow in India: sell an existing customer their next iPhone, persuade them to consider a Mac when they need a laptop, and earn from services in the years between those purchases.

Article Title: As JP Morgan and Charles Schwab say 'not allowed' to AI agents; Accenture warns: You are risking…
Article Text:
Consumers open to AI, but want control

Security concerns real, but not the whole story

'We've seen this movie before'

Banks still have a major role to play

Agentic flooding: an infrastructure challenge

Blocking AI agents may not work in the long run

As JPMorgan Chase, Charles Schwab and several major retailers move to keep personal AI agents out of their systems, consulting firm Accenture is warning that the strategy may backfire. According to a report by CNBC, Michael Abbott, Accenture's global banking lead, has warned that organisations risk falling behind if they focus on blocking AI agents instead of creating secure ways for them to interact with customers' accounts. “If customers explicitly authorize an AI agent to act on their behalf, that’s ultimately an extension of customer choice,” he said. The more important question, in his view, is not whether institutions can block agents but whether they can create a secure and trusted way for them to engage.As per the CNBC report, Abbott mentioned that the consumers are becoming open to using AI-powered tools to manage their financial activities, and the banks should view this as an opportunity rather than a threat. As per the Accenture Research report, around 64% of consumers are willing to use a GPT-like financial assistant via a generative AI platform or digital wallet and 71% would welcome an AI assistant integrated into their primary mobile banking app."If customers explicitly authorise an AI agent to act on their behalf, that's ultimately an extension of customer choice," Abbott said. He added that the more important issue for institutions is creating secure and trusted mechanisms for AI agents to engage with banking systems rather than attempting to block them outright.Asked to distinguish genuine security worries from companies protecting profits, Abbott said both can be true at once. He acknowledged “very real concerns around fraud, identity verification, liability and consumer protection,” adding that banks’ responsibility to safeguard customer assets and data does not disappear because an AI agent is involved. At the same time, he noted, consumers have historically benefited from technologies that improve transparency and make it easier to compare options.Drawing parallels with previous technology shifts, Abbott said the industry has experienced similar concerns during the rise of online banking, mobile banking and digital wallets. Consumers ultimately gravitated towards technologies that reduced friction and saved time, he noted."We've seen this movie before," Abbott said, arguing that institutions that adapt to changing customer behaviour typically emerge stronger than those that resist technological change. According to Abbott, the winners are usually the organisations that find safe ways to participate in new digital trends rather than trying to prevent them.Even as customer interactions increasingly move beyond bank-owned platforms and applications, Abbott believes financial institutions can remain central to the customer experience. He said banks have an opportunity to become trusted providers of data, intelligence and transaction execution for AI agents. As customers rely more on AI tools to make financial decisions, banks need to ensure they are present at critical decision-making moments, even if the customer is interacting through a third-party interface.On fears that millions of agents could overwhelm websites and customer-service systems, Abbott called it a possibility rather than a crisis. “I see it more as an infrastructure challenge than an existential threat,” he said, noting that most digital systems were designed for human interactions, while one person might soon have multiple agents continuously monitoring rates and comparing products. The answer, he said, is not to block agents but “to build the next generation of infrastructure that can authenticate trusted agents, verify permissions, manage identity and support machine-to-machine interactions efficiently. ” That, he added, is nothing new for banks: customers once interacted with them a couple of times a month and now do so nearly daily through mobile. “AI agents are just the next evolution. The organizations that prepare for that reality will be better positioned than those that try to prevent it.”Abbott also cautioned that AI-driven interactions could eventually operate at a scale far beyond what today's digital systems were designed to handle. Instead of blocking agents, organisations should focus on building infrastructure capable of authenticating trusted AI systems, verifying permissions and managing secure machine-to-machine interactions."AI agents are just the next evolution," Abbott said. "The organisations that prepare for that reality will be better positioned than those that try to prevent it."His comments come amid a broader debate across the financial services industry over how AI agents should interact with customer accounts. While some companies are restricting access because of security concerns, Accenture's view suggests that consumer demand and technological evolution may make resistance increasingly difficult over the long term.
Article Summary: Accenture's global banking lead Michael Abbott has warned that organisations risk falling behind if they focus on blocking AI agents. He added that the more important issue for institutions is creating secure and trusted mechanisms for AI agents to engage with banking systems rather than attempting to block them outright.

Article Title: Shark Tank judge Anupam Mittal questions ESOP tax rules; says employees are punished for ownership
Article Text:
Here’s what Anupam Mittal said

Shark Tank judge and Shaadi.com founder Anupam Mittal has questioned the country’s tax rules for Employee Stock Option Plans (ESOPs), saying employees are taxed heavily when they exercise their stock options and become shareholders. In a post on LinkedIn, Anupam Mittal argued that the tax system should encourage employee ownership instead of making it costly, especially as startups look to attract talent and create wealth. For those unaware, ESOPs allow employees to buy shares in a company at a fixed price, often giving them a chance to benefit as the business grows. However, when employees exercise their options, the difference between the purchase price and the market value of the shares is generally taxed as a salary perquisite at their applicable income tax rate.Anupam Mittal’s comments also come amid a recent Bengaluru Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) ruling involving a Flipkart employee. The tribunal held that proceeds from the company’s repurchase of vested but unexercised ESOPs could be taxed as long-term capital gains (LTCG), rather than as salary perquisites. However, the tax treatment depends on the structure and circumstances of the transaction.Sharing his views on X, Mittal wrote:“Why does India punish employee ownership?We keep telling employees - Think like an owner.Then we tax them for becoming one 🤷🏻Say you get ESOPs at ₹10.You exercise when the share is worth ₹100. That ₹90 appreciation can be taxed as a perquisite at your marginal rate, potentially ~40%.Why should emp wealth be treated less favourably than long-term wealth created by public or private investors?ESOPs aren’t compensation alone.They are how startups turn employees into owners, align incentives and spread wealth creation beyond founders and investors.If we believe India needs more startups, more employment generation & more wealth creation....then perhaps we should encourage ESOP ownership, not something we need tax lawyers for.Cheat code - If you can get your co to buy back your ESOPS instead of exercising them, recent case law suggests the gain qualifies for LTCG”
Article Summary: Shark Tank judge and Shaadi.com founder Anupam Mittal questioned the country’s tax rules for Employee Stock Option Plans (ESOPs) He said employees are taxed heavily when they exercise their stock options and become shareholders. Mittal argued that the tax system should encourage employee ownership.

Article Title: Zomato launches Host Mode, lets users hide menu prices from guests: Here’s how it works
Article Text:
Designed to make hosting more comfortable

How Host Mode works

Feature inspired by customer feedback

Food delivery platform Zomato has launched a new feature called Host Mode, aimed at making group food ordering more comfortable by hiding menu prices from guests while allowing hosts to retain control over the final bill. The new feature, which is now available to users across India, enables guests to browse restaurant menus and add dishes to the cart without seeing the cost of individual items. Hosts can later review the complete bill and place the order after authenticating with a passcode, fingerprint, or face lock.According to Zomato, the feature addresses a common social situation where guests often hesitate to order their preferred dishes when someone else is paying.The company said many diners tend to choose less expensive items or leave the decision to the host, while hosts typically want their guests to order freely without worrying about the cost.With Host Mode enabled, prices are removed from restaurant menus and the cart, allowing guests to focus solely on choosing what they would like to eat. The total bill remains hidden until the host decides to exit the mode and review the order.The company said the feature is particularly relevant during the festive season, when families and friends frequently gather and order food together.Users can activate the feature by tapping the Host Mode option available on the app's home screen, restaurant menu pages, or through the preferences section in their profile.Once enabled, prices disappear across menus and the cart, and guests can add items without seeing any pricing information. When the order is ready, the host can tap the option to exit Host Mode, authenticate using biometric verification or device security credentials, and view the complete bill, including any discounts or savings, before placing the order.Zomato said only the host can reveal the bill, ensuring that pricing details remain private throughout the ordering process.The company revealed that Host Mode originated from a suggestion shared by a Zomato customer on social media. According to Zomato, the idea was developed and rolled out on the app within 72 hours, with the goal of making social hosting and food ordering more seamless for customers. The launch adds to Zomato's ongoing efforts to introduce features aimed at improving user experience on its food delivery platform, particularly around social and group ordering occasions.
Article Summary: Zomato has launched a new feature called Host Mode, aimed at making group food ordering more comfortable by hiding menu prices. The new feature, which is now available to users across India, enables guests to browse restaurant menus and add dishes to the cart without seeing the cost of individual items.

Tech leaders continue to dominate the global wealth rankings, holding nine of the top 10 positions on the Forbes billionaires list released on November 1. However, a downturn across technology stocks over the past month erased a combined $273 billion from the fortunes of the world’s eight wealthiest individuals. A wave of disappointing corporate earnings and escalating market concerns over massive artificial intelligence (AI) expenditures pushed the tech-heavy Nasdaq down nearly 5%, triggering widespread declines among the industry's most prominent founders and executives. Notably, 9 out of 10 in list are tech executives, with Warren Buffett the only exception.Despite seeing their personal net worths shrink sharply, none of the top-ranking billionaires shifted position on the leaderboard.The planet's richest individual absorbed the steepest hit, shedding an estimated $68 billion. Musk's net worth stood at $869 billion. The decline came as an 11% drop in SpaceX shares, which outpaced a 13% gain in Tesla stock. Even after the contraction, Musk remains more than twice as rich as his closest competitor.Amazon founder Jeff Bezos has seen his net worth drop by an estimated $8 billion to $361 billion after Amazon shares fell 4%.Alphabet’s cofounders saw steep losses after shares of Google's parent company fell by more than 18%. Page dropped roughly $53 billion to sit at $233 billion, while Brin’s wealth shrank by about $49 billion to $214 billion.The bleeding continued for Dell Technologies and Meta. With Dell shares tumbling 21% and Meta sliding 15%, both Michael Dell and Mark Zuckerberg lost an estimated $40 billion each. Their net worths now sit at $229 billion and $211 billion, respectively.Bucking the tech market rout, only two billionaires in the global top 10 expanded their wealth over the past month, maintaining their ranks at the bottom of the elite bracket:Microsoft's former CEO saw his fortune tick up by $1 billion to an estimated $162 billion, supported by a 2% rise in Microsoft stock.The legendary Berkshire Hathaway investor was the month's biggest gainer among the top 10. A 9% jump in Berkshire shares boosted Buffett’s net worth by an estimated $13 billion to $154 billion.(Rankings and fortunes recorded as of November 1, 2026, at 12 a.m. ET)Notably, every member of the current top 10 is an American man. Six individuals hold net worths exceeding $200 billion, with the entry threshold for the elite group standing at $154 billion. Bill Gates dropped out of the top 10 in October 2024 following newly obtained financial disclosures that reduced his estimated net worth.Musk has retained the title of the world’s richest person since late May 2024, when he bypassed France’s Bernard Arnault. In June, Musk briefly made financial history by becoming the world's first trillionaire.Meanwhile, Jeff Bezos secured second place for the second straight month, a spot he previously occupied in May 2025. In September, Bezos became just the fourth person ever to cross the $300 billion threshold, joining Musk, Larry Page and Larry Ellison.Holding a fortune of approximately $133 billion derived from her stake in Walmart, she advanced to the 14th-richest position globally, up from No. 15 last month.
Article Summary: Tech leaders continue to dominate the global wealth rankings, holding nine of the top 10 positions on the Forbes billionaires list released on November 1. A downturn across technology stocks over the past month erased a combined $273 billion from the fortunes of the world’s eight wealthiest individuals. The planet's richest individual absorbed the steepest hit, shedding an estimated $68 billion.

Article Text:
Palmer Luckey, founder of Oculus and Anduril Industries

Palmer Luckey says he is not leaving California

What is California's Proposition 40

Yes, they should advocate against it No, they should support taxes for public welfare It depends on how the revenue is used 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Tech entrepreneur Palmer Luckey has said that the California’s proposed billionaire tax for its ultra-rich residents has caused friction between him and his friends. “This has been a point of friction between me and some of my other billionaire friends,” the 34-year-old cofounder of Oculus VR and Anduril said. “They’ve said things like ‘Palmer, you have to have solidarity for us. You can’t enable these really bad policies. If you stay and if you don’t leave, it’s going to show them that there’s no consequences.’ I empathize with that argument, but it’s not one that I’m going to participate in right now because I still believe that we can fix things.” For those unaware, California proposed a wealth tax bill earlier this year. It seeks to impose a one-time, 5% net-worth tax on California residents with a fortune exceeding $1 billion.Palmer Luckey said that while he opposes the bill, he is not leaving California unlike other tech entrepreneurs who have already left the state. Explaining why he thinks it is worth staying, he said during a press conference last week:“I think that this tax act, if you can call it a tax, is going to cause a lot of problems. It’s causing a lot of people to run who I don’t want to be running. It’s going to cause companies that I work with to leave the state, which is a problem for me.”“As of right now, though, I’m not running. I am staying,” he continued. “I think California is something special. I want to fight for California.”Proposition 40 will be on the ballot in November. It would impose a one-time 5% tax on California’s 200 billionaires. Ninety percent of the revenue would go to the state’s health care program. The remaining 10% would go to education, food assistance and administration. The bill has been opposed by several tech leaders including Google cofounders Sergey Brin and Larry Page, former Google CEO Eric Schmidt and PayPal cofounder Peter Thiel.
