Article Title: Jeff Bezos' $1 million grant is helping formerly incarcerated young people in Atlanta build farming businesses across 30 Black-owned farms and create 40 jobs
Article Text:
How Jeff Bezos' $1 million grant is supporting Atlanta's formerly incarcerated youth

How the programme combines farming with employment and training

Gangstas to Growers participants take part in hands-on farming activities in Atlanta. (Gangstas to Growers / Bezos Earth Fund)

How Gangstas to Growers is helping participants build businesses

Part of a $7.9 million investment in Atlanta's green spaces

What the organisation has achieved so far

A $1 million grant from Jeff Bezos' Bezos Earth Fund is supporting Gangstas to Growers, an Atlanta-based organisation that uses agriculture to create employment and entrepreneurship opportunities for at-risk and formerly incarcerated young people. Awarded in July 2023, the funding is intended to expand regenerative agricultural production across 30 farms on Black-owned land and create 40 new jobs. The initiative also aims to strengthen local food systems and generate economic activity in West Atlanta. By combining practical farming experience with business education and mentorship, the programme seeks to help participants develop marketable skills and explore pathways towards economic independence while supporting Black-owned farms and community-led food production.Gangstas to Growers, also known as G2G, is an Atlanta-based social enterprise founded by Abiodun Henderson. The organisation uses agriculture as a way to provide employment, entrepreneurship and personal-development opportunities to at-risk and formerly incarcerated young people.The initiative works with Black-owned farms around Atlanta, giving participants opportunities to learn agricultural skills through practical projects.Its approach combines farming with mentorship, business education and personal development, with the broader aim of addressing barriers to employment and reducing recidivism, which refers to returning to criminal behaviour or the criminal justice system after an earlier offence or period of incarceration.The Bezos Earth Fund awarded the $1 million grant in July 2023 to help the organisation expand its agricultural training and infrastructure. According to the fund, G2G plans to expand regenerative agricultural production across 30 farms on Black-owned land and create 40 new jobs for at-risk and formerly incarcerated young people.Participants learn practical agricultural skills, including seeding, growing, harvesting and composting. They receive opportunities to work on projects at Black-owned farms while gaining experience that can help them explore employment and entrepreneurship.The programme extends beyond agricultural instruction. Its curriculum also includes business education, mentorship, yoga, life coaching and arts classes. These activities are designed to help participants develop confidence, leadership abilities and skills that can be applied to different career paths.A December 2024 report by Georgia Public Broadcasting (GPB) documented how participants engage with the programme. It highlighted the experiences of young people who were developing agricultural skills while considering different professional ambitions.Not everyone intends to pursue farming as a full-time career. One participant featured in the report planned to pursue videography while continuing to grow plants at home. Another wanted to develop a business focused on helping people experiencing homelessness or housing insecurity.Beyond providing agricultural training, G2G aims to help participants develop businesses through worker-owned cooperatives. The model gives graduates opportunities to participate in collective ownership and build enterprises connected to local food production.One example is Sweet Sol, a hot sauce business associated with the organisation's graduates. Participants grow and harvest ingredients used to make the product, while the cooperative model connects agricultural production with food processing, product development and sales.According to G2G, proceeds support young people, the programme and Black-owned farms around Atlanta. The initiative demonstrates how agricultural training can lead to opportunities beyond farm work, including developing products and participating in small businesses.The organisation also works towards strengthening community ownership of food-related enterprises, allowing participants to explore business opportunities while contributing to the local economy.The $1 million grant was part of the Bezos Earth Fund's announcement of $7.9 million in funding for urban greening projects in Atlanta on July 17, 2023. The funding supported nine projects intended to improve access to green spaces and strengthen environmental conditions in underserved communities.The wider investment included initiatives involving urban farms, community gardens, native plants, wildlife habitats and agricultural workforce development. It formed part of the fund's $400 million Greening America's Cities initiative, which aims to improve equitable access to urban green spaces through 2030.Another recipient, On Da Farm, received $1 million to support urban farming, native plant cultivation, wildlife habitats and agricultural workforce development. Its plans included training 40 new farmers and 12 farmer apprentices, alongside producing food for local families through its weekly farmers' market.Gangstas to Growers' work fits into this broader strategy by connecting environmental sustainability with employment opportunities, food access and community economic development.Gangstas to Growers reports that its work has resulted in 5,000 pounds of food being harvested, 25 Black-owned farms being serviced and 20 programme graduates.These figures appear in the organisation's published impact summary and reflect its reported activities. Its website does not clearly specify the reporting period for each figure.The initiative has also received independent coverage. In December 2024, GPB reported on a graduating cohort, documenting how participants were developing agricultural skills and considering different career paths through the programme.The Bezos Earth Fund's grant announcement identifies expanding production across 30 Black-owned farms and creating 40 jobs as objectives of the investment. The available reporting does not establish whether these specific targets have been fully achieved.Through agricultural training, paid work and business development, Gangstas to Growers is seeking to create economic opportunities for young people who face barriers to employment while supporting Black-owned farms and strengthening Atlanta's local food system.
Article Summary: Gangstas to Growers is an Atlanta-based social enterprise founded by Abiodun Henderson. It uses agriculture to provide employment, entrepreneurship and personal-development opportunities to at-risk and formerly incarcerated young people. The initiative works with Black-owned farms around Atlanta, giving participants opportunities to learn agricultural skills. Its approach combines farming with mentorship, business education and personal development.

John Ternus’ first report card as Apple CEO beats Wall Street’s numbers, but the holiday quarter looks pricier to deliver. Apple’s revenue for the September quarter, the fourth of fiscal 2026, was $114.5 billion, up 12 percent and ahead of the $113.4 billion analysts expected. Earnings per share rose 14 percent to $2.10.The good mood lasted until Apple started talking about December. It expects gross margin of 45 to 46 percent, down from 47.9 percent, because memory chips keep getting more expensive, and it guided services growth at 8 to 9 percent, below what analysts wanted. Shares barely moved after the results, fell about 4 percent while the call was on, and settled around 2 percent lower.Ternus took over from Tim Cook on September 1, so this was his first call with analysts, and he did not do it alone. CFO Kevan Parekh was there, and so was COO Sabih Khan, a rare face on an Apple earnings call. Apple closed fiscal 2026 with record revenue of $478.8 billion, up 15 percent, and earnings per share of $8.98.iPhone revenue came in at $57.58 billion, up 17 percent and about $1 billion above estimates. Apple got there with only the iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max as new models, while the iPhone 17, iPhone Air and 17e filled out the lower end.So where was the standard iPhone 18? Ternus was asked exactly that and sidestepped it, saying Apple does not comment on future roadmaps.Apple also set September-quarter records for people upgrading their iPhones in the US, mainland China and India.Apple’s first foldable went on sale in October, so none of its sales show up in these results. It still took up much of the call. The Duo sold out online within hours, and delivery dates now stretch into next year. If you did not queue up on day one, you are waiting.Khan told analysts the Duo is “constrained as of today” and that it is hard to predict when supply and demand will balance. Ternus added that a very small percentage of units have come back over display issues, and Apple is replacing them. To widen supply, Apple is deepening its partnership with Perryman, the US titanium producer now supplying the phone.Apple rolled out Siri AI in beta for US English users in September and added French, Japanese, Korean, Portuguese and Spanish in October. On-device requests cost Apple almost nothing, Parekh said, but server-side requests carry inference costs that land in services cost of sales.Ternus said features that rely on server-side models, including Siri AI and intelligent photo editing, will have usage caps. People who need more will be able to buy expanded access, tied to iCloud+ plans. Apple has not shared pricing or the caps for each plan yet. Ternus also pitched privacy as Apple’s edge, noting that even Apple cannot see the personal data Siri taps into.Ternus called current memory pricing “unprecedented.” The 47.9 percent gross margin carried a boost of roughly one percentage point from tariff refunds. Strip that out and margin fell about a point from the June quarter, a drop Apple attributes entirely to memory.It gets harder from here. Parekh said memory costs will keep rising beyond December. Apple raised Mac and iPad prices at the end of June and iPhone prices in September, a move Parekh described as reluctant, and its manufacturing purchase obligations rose by $33 billion in the quarter.The December quarter will feel it. Mac and iPad supply will stay tight because of memory, with demand running higher than Apple expected.Services revenue rose 10 percent to $31.57 billion, an all-time high and in line with estimates. The App Store drew nearly a billion average weekly visitors, a record, and Apple now counts more than 1.5 billion paid subscriptions.The guidance is where it cools. Apple expects services growth of 8 to 9 percent in the December quarter, below the roughly 11 percent analysts expected. Parekh pointed to currency headwinds, third-party licensing, weak mobile gaming and a US court ruling that affects link-out transactions on the App Store.Mac revenue rose 24 percent to $10.79 billion, driven by the MacBook Neo and MacBook Pro, and Apple says it has never sold more Macs in a fiscal year. Full-year Mac revenue came to $37.9 billion, up from $33.7 billion. Apple also set a September-quarter record for people new to the Mac.The touchscreen MacBook Pro was only introduced last week, so it is not part of these numbers. Asked whether touch means iOS and macOS are heading toward one operating system, Ternus said no fundamentally different changes are planned, and that Apple would not talk about them anyway.Not every product kept up. iPad slipped 10 percent to $6.23 billion and wearables fell 8 percent to $8.3 billion, both against tough comparisons with last year’s product releases.India set an all-time revenue record for Apple, with the Mac also hitting all-time highs there. Apple Pay recently went live in the country with Axis Bank, which Ternus cited as an example of where services can still grow.Greater China told a more mixed story. Revenue grew 21 percent to $17.54 billion, a quarterly record, but that was about $1 billion short of what analysts had estimated. Parekh said supply constraints played a part.So Ternus walks into the holiday quarter with record sales behind him and memory costs ahead. Apple expects December to be its biggest quarter ever, with revenue up 7 to 10 percent, but higher chip prices will trim gross margin to 45 to 46 percent, and Mac, iPad and iPhone Duo supply will stay tight while demand runs ahead.
Article Summary: Apple set September-quarter records for people upgrading their iPhones in the US, mainland China and India. Apple closed fiscal 2026 with record revenue of $478.8 billion, up 15 percent, and earnings per share of $8.98. Apple expects gross margin of 45 to 46 percent, down from 47.9 percent.

Article Title: America's pharmaceutical industry is facing a 'monkey problem' and the reason is China, now a Palantir-backed tech startup plans to solve it
Article Text:
AI-generated image for representation purpose

Palantir co-founder's startup aims to tackle monkey problem of American pharmaceutical industry

Why is America facing a monkey shortage

Why are monkeys important for pharmaceutical research

America's pharmaceutical industry is facing a lab monkey crisis because of AI. A TechCrunch report says that the rising costs and restrictions on imports are adding pressure on laboratories. China has played a major role in supplying laboratory monkeys to the US. China, as stated in the report, accounted for nearly 60% of America's laboratory monkey imports before it banned exports in 2020. Facing supply constraints, American laboratories subsequently turned to Cambodia. However, a 2022 investigation found that wild-caught monkeys were falsely represented as captive-bred animals. Now, a startup backed by Palantir cofounder Joe Lonsdale plans to establish a large-scale monkey breeding facility in the US to help address the problem.As stated in the report, Safer Human Medicine, said to be backed by Joe Lonsdale aims to eventually breed 30,000 macaques over the next twenty years. The proposed facility is intended to reduce American laboratories' dependence on imported monkeys, which are widely used in pharmaceutical research and testing.The shortage has become more pressing as AI helps researchers discover potential drugs faster, increasing the number of experimental treatments that may need to be tested.However, the supply problem existed even before the recent growth of AI-assisted drug discovery.As mentioned above, China was one of the key suppliers of laboratory monkeys to the US. Since the export ban in 2020, the pharmaceutical industry has been hit with shortages. This in turn has also added to the cost.As stated in the report, macaques reportedly cost around $3,000 in 2019. But today their prices have since climbed to more than $20,000 with China reportedly charging approximately $26,000 per macaque.According to estimates, US laboratories import around 20,000 monkeys every year. Macaques are commonly used in medical experiments because of their biological similarities to humans. Researchers use them to study the safety, toxicity and biological effects of potential treatments before they move into human clinical trials.AI is also changing the drug discovery process. Researchers can use AI tools to identify potential medicines and generate more drug candidates in less time. However, promising candidates may still require laboratory studies, including animal testing, before human trials can begin.
Article Summary: Palantir co-founder's startup aims to tackle monkey problem of American pharmaceutical industry. Safer Human Medicine, said to be backed by Joe Lonsdale aims to eventually breed 30,000 macaques over the next twenty years. The proposed facility is intended to reduce American laboratories' dependence on imported monkeys.

Article Title: Disney may cut thousands of jobs; 'tells' managers: Make your target to ...
Article Text:
Disney layoffs: Managers asked to find 20% savings

Disney CEO Josh D'Amaro plans reinvestment

Disney lays off hundreds of employees, this is third round of job cuts this year

What did Disney CEO Josh D’Amaro tell shareholders

Walt Disney is considering cutting thousands of jobs and has asked some managers to target 20 percent in annual cost savings, Bloomberg News reported, citing people familiar with the matter. The savings could come from job eliminations as well as from reductions in other expenses, according to Bloomberg’s sources, who asked not to be identified because the discussions are private. The reported restructuring effort comes as Disney navigates multiple challenges, including the growing use of artificial intelligence, weaker box-office performance, intensifying competition from streaming rivals and a slowdown in international attendance at the company's theme parks.According to the report, Disney has directed some managers to target annual cost reductions of 20%. The savings could come from a combination of job cuts and other expense reductions across the business. The report added that not all parts of the company will be affected equally. Some Disney operations are expected to shoulder a larger share of the cuts than others as the company reviews spending across its businesses.The move comes under the leadership of Josh D'Amaro, who is reportedly seeking to redirect part of the savings into strategic growth areas. These include film and television programming, technology initiatives, theme parks and Disney's cruise business. The company has pledged to deliver double-digit growth in adjusted earnings per share during the current fiscal year, making cost controls and operational efficiency a key focus.In related news, Disney laid off hundreds of employees across several departments in September this year. The third round of job cuts this year mainly affected human resources and IT teams across Disney’s corporate operations and different business divisions. Announcing the job cuts, Disney CEO Josh D’Amaro and CFO Hugh Johnston shared a letter to the shareholders.The layoffs come after Disney warned shareholders in August that it was looking at more ways to reduce costs, including possible cuts to its workforce. The company had already announced major job reductions in April and July, followed by early-retirement offers to some longtime executives in August.Disney's latest layoffs come after D’Amaro and CFO Hugh Johnston signalled that more cost-cutting measures were being considered. In a letter to shareholders on Aug. 5, the executives wrote: “We remain highly focused on reducing costs across the enterprise to create incremental capacity to invest for growth and are evaluating a variety of levers, including reductions in labor and SG&A.” They added: “We are mid-stream in this work and will provide future updates on our progress. ” SG&A refers to selling, general and administrative expenses.
Article Summary: Walt Disney has asked some managers to target 20% in annual cost savings. The savings could come from job eliminations as well as from reductions in other expenses. The move comes under the leadership of Josh D'Amaro, who is reportedly seeking to redirect part of the savings into strategic growth areas.

Article Title: Bill Gates-backed sanitation technology has reached a Hyderabad park; a public toilet opened in September treats and reuses water on site, bringing years of research into an everyday public facility
Article Text:
Hyderabad becomes home to first public deployment

How it works

Backed by Gates Foundation and T-Works

Designed to recycle water on site

A technology that began as a global challenge

A sanitation technology backed by the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation has moved from years of research and development into everyday public use, with a new water-recycling public toilet now operating at Hyderabad's Lumbini Park. The facility, inaugurated in September, is designed to treat and reuse water on-site, reducing water consumption while offering a self-contained sanitation solution. The Net-Zero toilet, equipped with a water recycling system, was formally inaugurated by Telangana IT Minister Duddilla Sridhar Babu and Transport and BC Welfare Minister Ponnam Prabhakar, and the first such green toilet in the country is installed at the park.The installation at Lumbini Park marks the first public deployment of the ReFlow system, according to the company behind the technology. The unit was inaugurated in September 2026 by Telangana ministers and serves as a showcase for what ReFlow describes as closed-loop water infrastructure. The system is solar-powered, uses on-site water treatment and is designed for zero discharge operations.According to The New Indian Express, the facility was established at a cost of around Rs 1 crore and uses a water-recycling system that treats and reuses water multiple times rather than relying on conventional sewage infrastructure.ReFlow describes the unit as a containerised toilet with on-site treatment, designed not to discharge effluent. Instead of sending waste to a sewer or septic tank, the system treats water inside the container so it can be used again, and ReFlow’s pitch is that the toilet operates without a sewer connection. A Gates Foundation consultant, Vivek Pandey, cited the Lumbini Park unit at a recent Hyderabad event on wastewater as an example of treating wastewater where it is generated and reusing the recovered water for purposes such as flushing.The project was developed by environmental technology company ReFlow in collaboration with Telangana government's T-Works and the Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation. Hyderabad is also set to become a manufacturing hub for the technology, with the toilets expected to be supplied to other Indian states as well as international markets.The Gates Foundation has supported research into next-generation sanitation solutions for years, focusing on technologies that can safely process waste while reducing water use and infrastructure requirements. The Hyderabad deployment represents one of the latest efforts to bring those concepts into real-world public facilities.Unlike traditional public toilets that require connections to large-scale sewer and water networks, the ReFlow units are designed to operate with integrated water-treatment capabilities. The technology treats and recycles water within the facility, allowing it to be reused multiple times. The units can also be relocated and installed in different locations based on demand. ReFlow describes the system as a "closed-loop" model that combines sanitation with on-site treatment and water reuse, aiming to reduce strain on urban water resources while improving access to public sanitation.The effort belongs to a long-running Gates Foundation programme to reinvent the toilet. The foundation launched a “Reinvent the Toilet Challenge” to create sanitation solutions that need no sewer or septic connection and turn waste into safe byproducts. Georgia Tech’s second-generation reinvented toilet, known as G2RT, is one such project, and field testing has taken place around the world. The reports I found do not spell out which specific research the Hyderabad unit draws on.
Article Summary: New water-recycling public toilet now operating at Hyderabad's Lumbini Park. Facility, inaugurated in September, is designed to treat and reuse water on- site, reducing water consumption while offering a self-contained sanitation solution. Project was developed by environmental technology company ReFlow in collaboration with Telangana government's T-Works and Bill & Melinda Gates Foundation.
